protocol: Mayo experimental chamber series with variable ascent rate and prebreathe. Across 102 nested ascents to at least 30,000 ft, the total participants and person-exposures are unknown.
outcome_window: During described chamber runs. The authors report halting ascent when suggestive symptoms began. Postexposure monitoring is unspecified.
locator: Air Corps reprint, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 47)
note: The authors report no paralysis, loss of consciousness or symptom severity considered alarming in the series. Some less severe symptoms occurred, with their count unstated.

protocol: One selected chamber run with two subjects at 35,000 ft for two hours and fifteen minutes. Prebreathe and activity for this run are unspecified.
outcome_window: During the described 135-minute plateau. Postdescent follow-up was not reported.
locator: Air Corps reprint, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 46)
note: Both subjects had no reported untoward symptoms. One nested example within the overall Mayo scope.

protocol: Selected maximum-rate example. The subject walked at 2 mph for 30 minutes before ascent while continuously inhaling pure oxygen. Reported ascent rate was 4,700 ft/min. Peak altitude and dwell time in this example are unspecified.
outcome_window: Symptoms reported with this ascent. Follow-up window unspecified.
locator: Air Corps reprint, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 47)
note: One symptom-free subject described under the source endpoint. Linkage to the two-person prolonged run and position among the 102 ascents are unverified.

protocol: Two subjects in one selected chamber run. Each breathed pure oxygen at rest for 20 minutes. The source reports reaching 40,000 ft in 54 minutes at 722 ft/min. Start altitude and dwell time are unspecified.
outcome_window: Symptoms at 40,000 ft, with partial relief at 30,000 ft and subsequent recovery of remaining arm symptoms soon after reaching ground level.
note: One subject had severe right-hand joint pain. The other had neuritic arm pain and fatigue that stopped exercise. Both are symptomatic in this selected example. No separate trial roster or standardized clinical adjudication was reported.

protocol: Separate chamber experiment to 40,000 ft. The authors describe inadequate preliminary denitrogenation without a duration and report the cough after an alveolar air sample.
outcome_window: Cough appeared at altitude and lasted about two hours after descent. Chest soreness was reported for the next twenty-four hours.
note: A selected respiratory presentation discussed as characteristic of aeroembolism by the authors. The other subjects, denominator and clinical adjudication were not reported. Neither follow-up duration nor onset minute can be established.

protocol: Secondary quotation gives pressure at or below 197 mmHg and a reported altitude range of 10 to 14.5 km. The human exposure setting and individual pressure–gas histories are unspecified.
outcome_window: Joint pain described with low barometric pressure and relief after descent or pressure increase. Formal observation window unspecified.
note: Carson attributes 55 of 800 men and about 7 percent to Streltsov. The primary source is unavailable. Person-exposure count, diagnostic criteria and overlap with other series remain unresolved.
